rows.text: An eval is an automatic check that runs an agent's saved run and marks it based on guardrails, retries, and fallbacks. It ensures consistent results across different runs.
rows.label: wrong
rows.why: says an eval is based on guardrails, retries and fallbacks

rows.text: A pass bar shows whether the agent passes the checks. If it passes, the agent ships. If it fails, the agent retries.
rows.label: wrong
rows.why: says a failed pass bar makes the agent retry

rows.text: To check the reliability of the answers and identify weak spots.
rows.label: incomplete-but-true
rows.why: says reliability / weak spots, not that one run varies

rows.text: The LLM judge asks 5 times to ensure consistency and reliability. It averages the results to mitigate any single run's outlier.
rows.label: wrong
rows.why: says it averages; the lab says middle grade

rows.text: The wiring box "model" shows the internal workings of the agent, with boxes representing different components like the agent, tools, guardrails, and checks. It visualizes how the agent makes decisions and how it handles errors.
rows.label: wrong
rows.why: describes the agent's internals, not 'what happens behind the chat, drawn as clickable boxes'

rows.text: Tool precision measures how accurately the agent performs its tasks, focusing on the consistency and correctness of its actions. It ensures that the agent does not repeat unnecessary steps or make mistakes.
